announceDeregister(address).details: The operator stays in `X_all` and in `totalWeight` for the whole window and is      expected to keep signing. If it goes dark early the non-signer path absorbs its      absence, but its weight still counts toward the threshold denominator until the      change is committed — so announcing exits faster than the set can absorb them is a      liveness risk, not a safety one.

params.operator: the operator identity (`pointAddress(x, y)`) to remove on commit.

returns.index: queue position of the announced change.

announceRegister(uint256,uint256,uint256.details: The key is fully validated here — curve membership, weight bounds and proof of      possession — so an unusable announcement cannot sit in the queue and stall the      horizon. Nothing is added to `X_all` until the change is committed, so the announced      operator must not sign until then; its key would not be in the aggregate.

params.weight: stake weight to credit on commit.

returns.index: queue position of the announced change.

approvedRefBlock(bytes32).details: Reports unapproved once an operator-set change has moved `effectiveBlock` past the      approved `refBlock`, so a mid-transaction mutation fails closed.

cancelChange(address).details: Cancelling out of the middle leaves a hole rather than reordering, so the entries      around it keep both their positions and their `eligibleBlock`s — an unrelated      operator part-way through its notice window is not sent back to the start of it.      This is what keeps the forced paths usable: they refuse to act on an identity with a      queued change, and clearing that one entry no longer means cancelling everything      ahead of it. An emergency removal is `cancelChange(operator)` then      `deregisterOperator(operator)`, with no time gate between them.      Horizon-monotonic like `cancelNextChange`: removing a non-head entry leaves the      earliest `eligibleBlock` untouched, and removing the head can only move it later.

params.operator: the identity whose announced change should be dropped.

cancelNextChange().details: Only ever moves `nextPossibleMutationBlock()` later, never earlier, so it cannot      invalidate a round assembled against the horizon it published. Needed because an      abandoned announcement would otherwise pin the horizon and block every change behind      it in the queue.

commitNextChange().details: Changes commit in announcement order. Because `eligibleBlock` is non-decreasing in      that order, the head of the queue is always the earliest possible mutation, which is      what makes `nextPossibleMutationBlock()` a single storage read rather than a scan.

deregisterOperator(address).details: The escape hatch for an operator that must leave the set at once — a compromised key      cannot wait out a notice window. Carries the same lack of advance warning as the      immediate registration path, so `announceDeregister` is the routine way to remove an      operator and this is the exception.

params.operator: the operator identity (`pointAddress(x, y)`) to remove.

isValidSignature(bytes32,uint256,address.details: An operator-set mutation between the moment a round assembles its signature and the      moment the settlement is included makes that signature unusable. Which of two      failure modes a caller observes depends on when it pins `refBlock`:      - pinned **before** the mutation → `refBlock < effectiveBlock` and this reverts        `StaleSnapshot`.      - pinned **after** the mutation (the freshest-block strategy, `block.number - 1`) →        the watermark check passes, but the cached aggregate is no longer the one the        operators signed against, so verification fails and this returns `false`.      Both require the round to be re-assembled against the current set; neither can      admit a signature that was not valid for the set at `refBlock`.

params.nonSigners: operator identities that did NOT sign, strictly ascending.
params.refBlock: reference block; must be `>= effectiveBlock` and `< block.number`.

returns.ok: true iff the quorum signed and the signature verifies.

nextPossibleMutationBlock().details: A settlement is safe from set-mutation invalidation while the block it lands in is      below this value. It is a bound on the *scheduled* path only; the forced path can      mutate at any block.

registerOperator(uint256,uint256,uint256.details: The path to use while bootstrapping a registry that does not yet back any consumer,      when there is no round to invalidate. Once the registry is live, prefer      `announceRegister`: this invalidates any signature already assembled against the      pre-registration aggregate — a newly registered key cannot contribute to a round      already under way, and its presence in `X_all` is enough to break one — and it does so      without the advance warning `announceRegister` gives, so consumers relying on      `nextPossibleMutationBlock()` will be caught out. `ForcedMutation` marks the bypass      for off-chain consumers.

supportsInterface(bytes4).details: Consumers report `IGasKillerNested` only while their registry reports      `ISchnorrApprovalRegistry` here, so a router never plans a tree this cannot settle.

verifyAndApprove(bytes32,address,uint256.details: Expiry is checked here rather than by each frame, so no approval, and so no nested      frame, can exist after it whatever contract sits above that frame.

params.expiryBlock: the last block at which the tree may settle.
params.expiryProof: Merkle proof of the expiry leaf.
params.rootContract: the contract whose tree entrypoint settles the root.

aggX().notice: Running aggregate public key `X_all = Σ X_i` (identity = `(0,0)`).

announceDeregister(address).notice: Announce a deregistration, applicable once the notice window has elapsed.

announceRegister(uint256,uint256,uint256.notice: Announce a registration, applicable once the notice window has elapsed.

approvedRefBlock(bytes32).notice: Whether `root` was approved earlier in this transaction, and at which reference         block.

cancelChange(address).notice: Drop a specific identity's announced change, wherever it sits in the queue.

cancelNextChange().notice: Drop the oldest announced change without applying it.

commitNextChange().notice: Apply the oldest announced change once its notice window has elapsed.

deregisterOperator(address).notice: Deregister an operator immediately, bypassing the notice window.

effectiveBlock().notice: Block of the last operator-set mutation (verification fail-closes below this).

isValidSignature(bytes32,uint256,address.notice: Verify an aggregate Schnorr signature for `message`, accounting for the         declared non-signers.

nextPossibleMutationBlock().notice: The earliest block at which the operator set can change, or `type(uint256).max`         when nothing is announced.

noticeWindow().notice: Blocks that must pass between announcing a change and applying it.

operators(address).notice: operator Ethereum address (= address of its pubkey point) → operator record.

owner().notice: The registry owner, allowed to register operators (stands in for the         EigenLayer registration lifecycle).

pendingChangeCount().notice: Number of announced changes not yet committed or cancelled.

pendingChangeIndex(address).notice: Queue position of an identity's announced change, stored one-based so that zero means "nothing queued". Keeps both the duplicate-announcement check and cancelling a specific identity's change O(1), wherever it sits in the queue.

pendingChanges(uint256).notice: FIFO of announced-but-unapplied changes, `[pendingHead, pendingTail)`. `eligibleBlock` is non-decreasing in announcement order, so the head is the earliest block at which the operator set can next change. Cancelling out of the middle leaves a zeroed hole; `pendingHead` is always kept on a live entry (or equal to `pendingTail`) so reading the horizon stays a single storage load. A live entry's `operator` is never the zero address — it is either `pointAddress` of a key with a verified proof of possession, or an identity that had to be `registered` to be queued for removal — so zero marks a hole unambiguously.

pointAddress(uint256,uint256).notice: The Ethereum address of a public-key point (`keccak256(x‖y)[12:]`). This is         the operator identity used to look up non-signers.

popMessage(address).notice: The proof-of-possession message for an operator identity.

registerOperator(uint256,uint256,uint256.notice: Register an operator immediately, bypassing the notice window.

thresholdNum().notice: Threshold as a fraction `num/den` of total weight required to sign (e.g. 2/3).

verifyAndApprove(bytes32,address,uint256.notice: Verify a quorum signature over `root` and approve it for the rest of this         transaction.
